note: dev#87/#89/#91: bundled fallback list for suppressing false-positive Palworld version-mismatch warnings. 'known_versions' is the fast fingerprint path (Steam buildid + Pal-Windows.pak size, no pak content read, checked at every GUI startup). 'known_vanilla_manifest_sha256' is the dev#91 self-judgment path: the combined_hash from extract_vanilla.py's vanilla_manifest.json (sha256 over the small extracted output set, not the 37.7GB pak) — a future unknown Palworld build is treated as compatible if its extracted materials hash-match one of these, even though its build id/pak size do not appear in known_versions. dl.osakishokai.com/versions.json (dev#89) may extend all arrays via an optional top-level 'palworld_known_good' object with the same keys; on fetch failure or offline, the client falls back to this bundled file only. dev#1441: an optional top-level 'known_versions_conditional' array (same {build_id, pak_size, label} shape as 'known_versions', plus a required 'min_tool_version' string, e.g. "2.11.0") expresses "this Palworld build is only verified-good from tool version X.Y onward". Deliberately a SEPARATE top-level key, not additional fields inside 'known_versions': clients older than dev#1441 only ever read the 'known_versions' key and would silently ignore an unrecognized 'min_tool_version' field, unconditionally whitelisting the build for every tool version (fail-unsafe). Because old clients never look at 'known_versions_conditional' at all, they simply don't get the benefit of a conditional entry (they keep showing the generic mismatch warning) instead of misjudging it as safe. New clients (app_py\compat_check.py evaluate(), given their own TOOL_VERSION) suppress the warning only when TOOL_VERSION >= min_tool_version; otherwise they still warn, plus show an additional 'updating this tool may resolve it' hint (i18n key MsgPalworldVersionUpdateHintFormat). This bundled file has no 'known_versions_conditional' key at all right now (no build has needed it yet, and merge_known_good()/parse_known_versions_conditional() both treat a missing key the same as an empty list) — this note only documents/reserves the schema for when a future build needs it.
